localFacts.fact: funda's article for estate agents on 360° photos says distortion often comes from the camera moving between frames, so always use a tripod to keep the camera still.
Photofacts (Liesbeth van Asselt) gives the rule of thumb that camera plus lens should weigh at most half the tripod's load capacity for optimal stability.

Dutch Auteurswet art. 18 allows images of works made to stand permanently in public places to be reproduced and published as they are there. General information, not legal advice: shoot exteriors from the public street.
Benro Europe publishes 153 cm maximum height with the centre column retracted for the TMA38CL, a figure the US page leaves out.
Dutch terms: tandwielkop / geared head, 3-wegkop, balhoofd, middenzuil, nivelleerbasis, snelkoppelingsplaat; Arca-Swiss keeps its name.

localPainPoints.pain: A ball head sags a little after locking, which spoils a carefully levelled frame.
localPainPoints.fix: A geared head (Manfrotto 410 or 405) moves each axis by knob and holds the position; that is the English post's head advice.

quotes.text: dan zakt de camera altijd nog iets door na het vastzetten van het balhoofd. Dus daar gaat je compositie.
Als je niet wilt dat je statiefkop nog even zakt, moet je een geared head nemen.

localPainPoints.pain: A raised centre column loses a lot of stability.
localPainPoints.fix: Pick by column-down height and keep the column down; interiors only need about 1,2 to 1,5 m.

quotes.text: Hij verliest wel enorm aan stabiliteit als de middenzuil in de hoogste stand staat.

localGain.point: funda's own advice to always use a tripod for 360° photos, linked to the leveling-base section.
Photofacts' half-the-load rule of thumb for the load checklist.
